title: The Job — Sc019: amazed two-shot on a photographic background plate

source.github: mhvnsnt/cn-gigaleak-gumball, draft release untagged-1676e192ae8c72e95791, asset id 640772406
source.method: FLA (XFL zip) read via sequential local-header parser (2012 Flash zips have malformed central directory); DOMDocument.xml + LIBRARY symbol XMLs parsed directly. Same neutral per-keyframe transform format as production/dance-choreo v1: a part pose is (item, first_frame, affine matrix a/b/c/d/tx/ty, pivot). keyMode 9728 = pose-to-pose; sampled_frames hold each keyframe's elements to the next keyframe, matching SWF playback.

teaches: Two-character close interaction over a PHOTO plate: the background is a real photograph of a house and picket fence (Gumball's mixed-media signature), and both puppets play a 'squee' reaction — hands pressed to cheeks, star-pupil eyes — stacked as separate scene layers (DARWIN over the Gumball puppet layer). The comedy timing is offset: Darwin holds the delight for the whole 56 frames while Gumball's face falls to a worried blank stare around frame 35. Same frame, two reaction clocks.
notes: Background is a photographic plate, not a painted BG — the flat vector puppets are composited over it on the 'background' layer.
Eye/mouth comps (EYESCOMP2/MOUTH2, 199-223 kf each) carry the scene; bodies are nearly still. In close-up, the face system IS the animation.
Darwin's squee never breaks; Gumball's drops at ~f35 — offsetting reaction timing between characters in the same shot is the joke's engine.
Second-generation comps (the '2' versions) are used: the library keeps versioned face systems per production block.
